title: FileShare - Path Traversal (Easy)
description: Exploit unvalidated file path parameters in download and preview endpoints to read arbitrary files outside the web directory.
hints: Inspect the query parameter passed to /api/download and /api/preview.
The server does not validate or sanitize relative directory tokens. Use '../../../../app/flag_traversal.txt' to extract the flag.

title: FileShare - Path Traversal (Medium)
description: Bypass a single-pass path traversal filter that strips '../' tokens from file paths.
hints: The application executes a single-pass string replacement stripping '../'.
Nested patterns like '....//' collapse into '../' after the single replacement, or URL encoded sequences like '%2e%2e%2f' evade the filter.

title: FileShare - Path Traversal (Hard)
description: Bypass recursive directory traversal filters or path prefix validation to extract the secret flag file.
hints: The download filter requires paths to start with 'uploads/' or recursively strips '../'.
Satisfy the required prefix while traversing back out using 'uploads/../../app/flag_traversal.txt' or test double URL encoding (%252e%252e%252f).

title: FileShare - Unrestricted File Upload (Easy)
description: Upload a Python script directly without file extension or content restrictions and trigger execution via the script runner.
hints: The /api/upload endpoint allows any file extension, including .py and .sh.
Upload a script that reads environment variables and use the /api/execute endpoint to trigger it.

title: FileShare - Unrestricted File Upload (Medium)
description: Bypass a naive extension blacklist restricting .py and .sh files to achieve script execution.
hints: The upload endpoint blocks filenames ending with exact lowercase extensions .py or .sh.
Check how case sensitivity or alternate script extensions (.PY, .py3, .phtml) are handled by the validator and runner.

title: FileShare - Unrestricted File Upload (Hard)
description: Achieve server-side code execution by exploiting filename path traversal or Zip Slip archive extraction to drop an executable plugin.
hints: Direct uploads to the uploads folder enforce a strict whitelist, but the server retains a path traversal in the filename parameter.
Upload a file with filename='../../plugins/exploit.py' or provide a zip archive with directory traversal entries to drop files into the plugins directory, then run it via /api/plugins/run.

title: FileShare - Weak MIME Validation (Easy)
description: Bypass client-side MIME type verification by spoofing the Content-Type HTTP header during image upload.
hints: The image upload endpoint /api/upload/image validates the client's Content-Type header without inspecting file contents.
Use curl's ';type=image/png' option to upload non-image content disguised as a valid PNG.

title: FileShare - Weak MIME Validation (Medium)
description: Bypass magic byte verification by constructing a polyglot file containing valid image headers and an executable script payload.
hints: The server verifies the leading magic bytes (e.g. GIF89a or PNG header) but ignores the rest of the file.
Prefix your script payload with the 6-byte string 'GIF89a;' and upload as a GIF.

title: FileShare - Weak MIME Validation (Hard)
description: Exploit XML External Entity (XXE) injection within the SVG vector image parser to read protected server secrets.
hints: The image gallery accepts SVG vector files and processes them with an XML engine configured with external entity resolution enabled.
Embed a DOCTYPE declaration with an ENTITY pointing to 'file:///app/flag_mime_hard.txt' within an SVG file.
